_comment: AJMN ENGAGEMENT requirements register (the WHY), DERIVED FROM the customer's own human-authored Solution Design Document (AJMN SDD, 18 May) + NRFU. Pass with --requirements requirements.aj.json so the published design_blueprint right-sizes to the real AJMN target (Cisco Nexus 9000 VXLAN BGP-EVPN Multi-Site fabric). Grounded, not invented: keys the SDD does NOT state (a numeric convergence budget, a target supernet, an explicit VLAN-to-zone map) are deliberately OMITTED so the blueprint surfaces them as honest open questions rather than fabricating them.
_provenance: SDD sections: 'Design Overview / Multi-Site Design', 'AJMN Physical Architecture' (seven CARs), 'Current AJMN Core and Critical Network Architecture' (IPTV/MSN/DMZ/IE/WE segments), 'Shared Border' (Firewall + Load Balancer), 'Out-of-Band Management', 'Migration Approach - High Level'.

requirements.growth_horizon: Multi-Site VXLAN BGP-EVPN fabric across seven sites (CARs) in one campus; scale-out east-west by adding spines/leaves; replaces the legacy 3-tier Catalyst 6807-XL core + 4500X/4948 aggregation/access
constraints: Standardize on Cisco Nexus 9000 / NX-OS, managed by Nexus Dashboard (NDFC + NDI)
Overlapping DC/BC VLAN IDs require port-VLAN translation to a new fabric VLAN/VNI
Legacy<->fabric migration uses a single logical L2 handoff per VLAN (the EVPN fabric does not forward STP BPDUs)
Out-of-band management on physically separate gear; it must not transit the fabric it manages
Multi-window, NRFU-gated cutover; the fabric must be fully deployed and tested before any workload migration
